title: Top 9 Food Labels That Actually Matter(And What To Ignore!)
summary: A grocery-label guide that recommends organic produce, dairy and chicken, pasture-raised eggs and grass-finished beef, and warns about glyphosate.

assertions.quote: which of course means that it's not sprayed with any chemicals or pesticides, right? No.
They use more natural, less harsh ones like plant extracts and microbes
So, the food grown studies show has more nutrition for you and I.
When you're not spraying the synthetic pesticides in the soil, it's healthier.
I really like to lean on something called the dirty dozen list
hormones have not been allowed in chickens from the 1970s
Both chickens never ever go outside. They live in a warehouse, but one is getting a conventional feed and one is getting an organic feed.

verdicts.note: Organic rules require outdoor access and other living conditions for poultry, although in practice outdoor areas can be small.

EU organic standards require livestock to be reared outdoors for part of the year and give pigs and poultry access to forage, though in many regions organic poultry get conserved forage only; EU rules, not US.

Organic poultry rules go beyond feed: 7 CFR 205.238 requires conditions for exercise and freedom of movement and bans de-beaking and induced molting; the excerpt omits the avian outdoor-access rules, so it does not show how indoor conditions actually differ.

assertions.quote: Free range, my friends, literally means almost nothing.
nutritionally speaking, they're way superior eggs compared to freerange or cage-free

verdicts.note: Pastured hens' eggs tend to have more omega-3, vitamin E and carotenoids, but the size of the difference varies and it is modest for overall nutrition.

assertions.quote: grass-fed meat is nutritionally superior to grain-fed
you would think that means it's 100% grass-fed. No.

verdicts.note: Without a 100 percent grass-fed or grass-finished claim or certification, cattle labelled grass-fed may have been finished on grain.

assertions.quote: you're literally dousing it in glyphosate, which is linked to many, many health issues
